chunks: From another book: I saw you, may Allah prolong your honor, in contemplation of my letter, and bestowing what is easy for me to add to your other favors upon me. I requested, may Allah prolong your honor, that you ask some of the jurists about the worshipper when he rises from the first Tashahud for the third Rak'ah: is it obligatory for him to recite the Takbir? For some of our companions said: It is not obligatory for him to recite the Takbir, and it suffices for him to say: 'By the power and might of Allah, I rise and I sit.'

The answer: He said: Indeed, there are two traditions in this matter. As for one of them, it is that when he transitions from one state to another, he must recite the Takbir. As for the other, it is narrated that when he raises his head from the second Sajdah, he recites the Takbir, then sits, then stands; thus he does not need to recite the Takbir for standing after sitting. And the first Tashahud follows this same pattern. Whichever of the two you follow regarding the Taslim, it is correct.

And regarding the ring of the goldsmith, is it permissible to pray wearing it if it is on his finger? The answer: There is dislike (Karahah) in praying wearing it, and there is also permissibility (Itilaq). The practice is upon the dislike.

And regarding a man who bought a sacrificial animal (Hady) for an absent man and asked him to sacrifice on his behalf in Mina, but when he wanted to slaughter the animal, he forgot the man's name and slaughtered the animal, then remembered him afterwards. Does it suffice for the man or not? The answer: There is no problem with that, and it has sufficed for his companion.

And among us are weavers of the Majus (Zoroastrians) who eat carrion and do not perform Ghusl from Janabah, and they weave clothes for us. Is it permissible to pray in them before they are washed? The answer: There is no problem in praying in them.

And regarding the worshipper who is in the night prayer in darkness, and when he prostrates, he mistakes the prayer mat and places his forehead on a cloth or rug. When he raises his head, he finds the prayer mat. Does he count this Sajdah or not? The answer: As long as he has not sat upright, there is no problem for him in raising his head to seek the cover (Turbah/Sajdah place).

And regarding the Muhrim who raises the shades; does he raise the wood of the canopy or the church and raise the wings or not? The answer: There is no problem for him in leaving them, and all the wood.

And regarding the Muhrim who shades himself from the rain with a sack or other thing, so that his clothes and what is in his load do not get wet. Is that permissible? The answer: If he does that in the load on his way, he must offer Dam (sacrifice).

And the man performs Hajj as a proxy (for a fee). Does he need to mention the one whose Hajj he is doing at the time of contracting his Ihram or not? And is it obligatory that he must slaughter a sacrifice for the one whose Hajj he is doing and for himself, or does one Hady suffice for him? The answer: He mentions him, and if he does not, there is no problem. And is it permissible for the man to enter Ihram in a fur cloak or not? The answer: There is no problem with that, and righteous people have done it.

And is it permissible for the man to pray with slippers (Battit) on his feet that do not cover the ankles, or not? The answer: It is permissible. And the man prays with a knife or an iron key in his sleeve or trousers; is that permissible? The answer: It is permissible.

And regarding a man who is with some of these people, and their companion performs Hajj and takes the main road, and these do not enter Ihram from Maslakh. Is it permissible for this man to delay his Ihram until Dhat Irq so that he enters Ihram with them for fear of being seen, or is it not permissible for him to enter Ihram except from Maslakh? The answer: He enters Ihram from his Miqat, then puts on the clothes and recites the Talbiya softly in himself. When he reaches their Miqat, he makes it audible.
And regarding wearing the leather shoes (Mu'atwan), for some of our companions mention that wearing it is disliked. The answer: That is permissible and there is no problem with it.

And regarding a man who is one of the trustees of the Waqf (endowment), who considers permissible what is in his hand and does not refrain from taking his wealth. Perhaps he stays in a village while he is there, or enters his house and his food is prepared. He invites me to it. If I do not eat his food, he becomes hostile to me and says: 'So-and-so does not consider it lawful to eat our food.' Is it permissible for me to eat his food and give charity for it? And what is the amount of the charity? And if this trustee gives a gift to another man and it is presented to me, and I invite me to partake of it, and I know that the trustee does not refrain from taking what is in his hand (from the endowment), is there anything upon me if I partake of it? The answer: If this man has wealth or livelihood other than what is in his hand, then eat his food and accept his gift. Otherwise, do not.

And regarding a man who is among those who speak the truth and believe in Mut'ah (temporary marriage) and believe in Raj'ah (return), except that he has a wife who agrees with him in all his affairs, and he made a covenant with her that he would not marry another over her, nor do Mut'ah, nor take a concubine. And he has done this for about fifteen years and fulfilled his word. Perhaps he is absent from his house for months, so he does not do Mut'ah, and his soul does not stir for it either. And he believes that the presence of those with him from brothers, sons, servants, trustees, and retinue reduces him in their eyes, and he loves to remain as he is out of love for his family and inclination towards them and guarding them and himself. He does not forbid Mut'ah, but he considers it a duty to Allah. Is there any sin upon him in leaving it or not? The answer regarding that: It is recommended for him to obey Allah in Mut'ah so that the oath of knowledge (or specific knowledge) is removed from him even if only once.

If you consider it proper, may Allah prolong your honor, to ask for me regarding that and explain it to me and answer in each question with what is to be acted upon, and confer the favor upon me in that, may Allah make you the cause for all good and execute it through your hand, so you will be rewarded, if Allah wills. May Allah prolong your life and preserve your honor and support and happiness and safety and dignity, and perfect His blessing upon you and increase in His goodness to you, and make me a ransom for you from evil, and precede me for you and accept you. All praise is to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah bless Muhammad the Prophet and his family abundantly.

key_terms.التَّشَهُّدُ الْأَوَّلُ: The first Tashahud (sitting for testimony in prayer)

ai.seo_question: What are the rulings on Takbir during prayer transitions and praying in clothes of the Majus?
ai.summary: This excerpt from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* captures the jurisprudential dialogue between Imam al-Hadi (AS) and his representative Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ja’far Himyari, addressing nuanced issues in *Salat* and *Hajj*. It highlights the Shia methodology of reconciling apparent contradictions in hadith, such as the obligation of Takbir during transitions in prayer, and demonstrates the practical application of rulings on ritual purity and social ethics, including the permissibility of praying in garments woven by Majus.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 346 - In another book, a letter is mentioned containing the following questions, which were written to a special envoy of Imam Mahdi (a.s):  Question: May the Almighty Allah continue your respect and honor; ask the Faqih (Imam Qaim) following questions and inform me: When a worshipper gets up after reciting the first Tashahud to recite the third Rakat, is it obligatory for him to recite the Takbir? Because some of our scholars say that it is not obligatory, on the contrary he is allowed to say Bihawlillaahi Quwwatihi aqoomo wa aqud.

Reply: There are two traditions in this connection: the first is that when the worshipper lifts his head from Sajdah he recites the Takbir, then he sits and then he stands up; thus he does not need to recite the Takbir for standing up after sitting. The same is with the case of the first Tashahud. One can choose any of the options.
Question: Also please inquire if one can pray wearing a ring of Hadid? Reply: It is detestable (Makruh).

Question: A person bought a sacrificial animal on behalf of a person who was not present as the latter had told him to sacrifice in Mina on his behalf; but when he wanted to slaughter the animal, he forgot the name of that person and he remembered it only after the sacrifice; is it a proper procedure for the person who delegated the ritual? Reply: There is no problem; the sacrifice was complete.

Question: There are some Majusi weavers among us who eat carrion and don’t perform bath (Ghusl) of Janabat; can we pray in the clothes weaved by them without purifying them? Reply: There is no problem in it.

Question: A person is reciting Midnight Prayers in dark; when he goes into Sajdah, his forehead falls on something other than the place of prostration; that is the floor etc. Now when he raises his head, he finds the Turbah; does he have to count that Sajdah? Reply: Till he does not sit upright, he can raise his head to search for the Turbah.

Question: A person who is wearing Ihram removes the covering of the canopy, but leaves the frame. Is it allowed? Reply: There is no problem if he leaves the frame. One of the things a person in Ihram has to avoid is shade. Thus, if he rides a camel with a canopy or a bus with roof, he has to pay the Penalty (Kaffarah) of sacrificing a sheep, but if the covering of the canopy or the bus is removed, leaving the frame and walls, there is no problem in it.

Question: If a person wearing Ihram shades himself with a sack or with something else to protect himself or his seat from getting soaked in rain, is it allowed for him to do so? Reply: If he does this on the way with canopy, the Kaffarah is obligatory on him. The penalty of a goat is due to the fact that the person has shaded himself from rain and to shade oneself is an omission for a person in Ihram.

Question: Is it necessary for a person doing Hajj as proxy, to mention the name of the one whose Hajj he is doing at the time of Ihram? Is it obligatory that he must make separate sacrifice for himself as well as whose Hajj he is performing? Reply: It is not necessary to recite it in detail and one sacrifice is sufficient on behalf of the one whose Hajj he is performing.
Question: Is it permitted for man to tie up the Ihram with a sheet of fur? Reply: There is no problem; righteous and decent people have dressed (been Muhrim) in it.
Question: Is it permitted for man to keep with himself an iron knife or an iron key while praying? Reply: It is allowed.

Question: A man goes for Hajj with a group of Sunnis and they do not put on the Ihram at Maslakh. Whether this man is allowed to delay his Ihram till Zaat-e-Arq so that he becomes Muhrim with them at that place? Reply: It is necessary to become Muhrim from the Miqaat and say the Thalbiya softly and when he reaches the Miqaat with them, he should make it obvious.
Question: How is wearing leather slippers, because people say that it is Makruh to wear them? Reply: It is permissible and there is no problem.

Question: A man is a treasurer in endowments and he is careless. He considers as permissible for himself the endowments, which are under his control, and he does not abstain from them. Often when I enter his office and he is present or I enter his house and he is present, he invites me to eat and if I don’t eat at his place, he would become inimical to me and say: such and such has not considered my food lawful. Now please tell me if it is allowed for me to eat with him and then later pay Sadaqah for it. And how much Sadaqah should I pay? Or whether it is allowed for me to accept a gift from him? Reply: If this man is having other property in addition to the endowments he holds and has other occupations as well, you may eat with him and accept his gifts. If it is not so, you must neither eat at his place nor accept any gift from him.

Question: A man is a Shia and considers Mutah and temporary marriage permissible and also believes in the Rajat (return) and all his family members are united. This man has made a vow that he would neither take a second wife nor do Mutah. And he has spent 19 years with this vow. Now if he breaks his vow, does he become liable for a penalty or sin? Reply: It is Mustahab (recommended) for him to do Mutah at least once for obedience of Allah, so that the sin of the vow is removed from him. [This letter is followed by the discourse of Husain bin Rauh as follows:] Thus if you consider it proper, may Almighty Allah strengthen your honor, ask these questions from Imam (a.s) and leave their explanation for me and write to me the command in each issue and leave your favor on me. May the Almighty Allah deem you as the channel of all good and may He issue it through you. If you do this, you would have performed a preferred and a rewardable act. May Almighty Allah give you a long life, may He preserve your respect and good fortune and complete His bounties on you and may He increase His favors on you. May He deem me your ransom in every calamity and may He fix my death before you. All praise is from the Lord of the worlds and exceeding benedictions be on His Messenger, Prophet Muhammad (s) and his family.
